title: OpenDEA Benchmark Comparison
description: A governed, reproducible derivation over the admitted members of a BenchmarkCohort (CR-AM-07 §3). A BenchmarkComparison answers 'how do we compare it?' — distribution, percentile, rank, and peer position — consuming CR-AM-06 eligibility without redefining it. A comparison is a derived artifact, never the truth: the truth is the set of eligible AssessmentResults, and the same cohort snapshot must always reproduce the same comparison (CR-AM-07 §10). This schema defines the comparison shape only — the distribution engine (Phase 2) and percentile/ranking engine (Phase 3) are runtime concerns.

cohort.description: The BenchmarkCohort this comparison derives from, pinned to a membership snapshot so the derivation is reproducible (CR-AM-07 §3). Membership itself is governed exclusively by CR-AM-06 — this object references the cohort, it does not admit members.

membership_hash.description: Content hash of the admitted membership at snapshot time. The hashing method is declared in derivation.notes; same membership must always produce the same hash.

comparability_key.description: Inherited verbatim from the cohort (CR-AM-07 §3). Comparison never widens the comparability key.

comparison_axis.description: The single score axis standings are computed on — never a mixture of axes (CR-AM-07 §5).

distribution.description: Population statistics over the admitted members on the comparison axis (CR-AM-07 §4). Emitted only when the cohort's minimum_sample_size is satisfied — small-population statistics are never silently emitted (CR-AM-07 §4, §10).

n.description: Admitted population size included in this distribution.

q1.description: First quartile of the distribution on the comparison axis.

q3.description: Third quartile of the distribution on the comparison axis.

standard_deviation.description: Optional spread measure. Sample standard deviation unless derivation.notes declares otherwise.

standings.description: Per-member standing within the cohort (CR-AM-07 §5, §6). Tied members share the same percentile and rank under the declared derivation rules — ties are never broken by member identity.

member.description: The AssessmentResult this standing belongs to.

score.description: The member's value on the comparison axis.

percentile.description: Standing within the cohort distribution under the declared percentile_method (CR-AM-07 §5).

rank.description: Ordinal standing under the declared ranking_rule (CR-AM-07 §6).

derivation.description: How this comparison was produced (CR-AM-07 §3, §10). Every methodological choice is declared; nothing is implicit.

minimum_sample_size.description: The cohort's minimum sample size enforced for this derivation (CR-AM-06 §6, CR-AM-07 §10).

minimum_sample_satisfied.description: MUST be true whenever distribution is present. A comparison with minimum_sample_satisfied=false is refused, not emitted (CR-AM-07 §10).

excluded_members.description: Admitted members excluded from the distribution with an explicit reason — missing data is N/A, never zero (CR-AM-07 §10 constraint 2).

reproducibility_hash.description: Content hash of the derivation inputs. Same cohort snapshot must produce the same comparison (CR-AM-07 §10 constraint 1). The hashing method is declared in notes.
